findings.claim: No test exercises the code that the r1 fix changed: the release of the library's `focusing` flag and the ownership check in `releaseOfficeGrid`. Every Excel mock in the tests lacks an `xs.sheet`, so `releaseGridFocus` and `focusProbe` do nothing there.
findings.impact: Suppose `releaseGridFocus()` were dropped from `onFocusIn`, or `releaseOfficeGrid` cleared the probe and the active flag without checking ownership. CI would still pass. A user would hit the first mutation as I10 breaking: they click the grid, press Ctrl/Cmd+F, then paste into the find field, and x-data-spreadsheet's window `paste` handler calls preventDefault on it. They would hit the second as I8 breaking: a cancelled earlier Excel load resets a later viewer's state, and ← / → then change file while the grid is active. The spec assigns I9 and I10 to R-5 (manual), so this is a gap in the safety net, not a spec violation.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/office/excelAdapter.ts:27-30 writes `spreadsheet.xs.sheet.focusing`, and :73-74 installs the probe only when `spreadsheet.xs` exists. frontend/src/components/__tests__/FilePreview.officeArrowKeys.test.tsx:29-47 and FilePreview.office.test.tsx:80-93 return `{preview, destroy}` with no `xs`. The test "change file again after a click outside the grid" passes only through the `focusin` path, because the outside button takes focus in `clickOn`. A grep of frontend/src for `releaseOfficeGrid` and `focusing` finds no test. I read the library source (node_modules @js-preview/excel/lib/index.js) and confirmed that `focusing` lives on `xs.sheet` (`this.sheet=new hn(...)`) and that it gates the window paste, copy and keydown handlers.
findings.repro: Mutation by reading: delete line 69 `releaseGridFocus();` in excelAdapter.ts. Nothing in the listed tests fails, because no mock exposes `xs.sheet.focusing`. Mutation: change `releaseOfficeGrid` to set `focusProbe = null; active = false` unconditionally. No listed test fails either.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is broken today. The fix since r1 has no test, and by the spec I9 and I10 are checked by hand only.

findings.proposed_fix: Give the Excel mock in FilePreview.officeArrowKeys.test.tsx an `xs.sheet` with a `focusing` flag. Set the flag on a grid click and clear it on a window click outside, as the library does. Then assert: (a) after focus moves to the comment input, `focusing` is false; (b) after unmount, `focusing` is false; (c) when a stale viewer is disposed after a newer one has drawn, the newer viewer's arrow gate stays in force.

findings.claim: When a menu is open, a press on the Excel grid closes the menu and the library selects a cell on mousedown. DismissScrim then swallows the click in the document capture phase, so neither `onClickInside` nor the library's window click handler sees it. The grid shows a selected cell, but ← / → change file instead of moving that cell.
findings.impact: The user opens the ⋮ menu (or any DismissScrim popup) and closes it by clicking a cell. The cell looks selected, and the next → goes to another file. Commit caf19847 tried to fix this defect and commit beae9a97 reverted that attempt, which leaves the defect open with no test. The behaviour does match the stated definition of an 'active' grid, because no click reached it.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/DismissScrim.tsx:41-45 and :59: a capture-phase `swallow` on document calls stopPropagation on the click. frontend/src/components/office/excelAdapter.ts:60-63, 71: `onClickInside` is a bubble listener on the container. In the library, `W(window,"click",…focusing=t.contains(e.target))` is a window bubble listener. The revert message for beae9a97 says selection starts on mousedown.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. By reading: open the file's ⋮ menu, click a grid cell, then press →. Expected from the code: the menu closes, the cell is highlighted, and the file changes.

bucket_proposal.reason: I8 defines 'active' as starting with a click inside the grid. The swallowed click never reaches the grid, so I8 holds as written. The result still reads wrong to a user: a visibly selected cell while the arrows change file.

findings.proposed_fix: Decide whether a dismissing press on the grid should select a cell. If not, stop the grid's mousedown while a DismissScrim swallow is armed. If so, accept the behaviour and record it.

specification_compliance: The r1 finding (a synthetic body click reaching app-wide listeners) is resolved. `releaseGridFocus` now writes `spreadsheet.xs.sheet.focusing = false` directly (excelAdapter.ts:27-30). The library source confirms that `focusing` is a field of `xs.sheet` and that it gates the window paste, copy and keydown handlers. No event is dispatched any more.

`releaseOfficeGrid` (officeGridActive.ts:23-26) clears the probe only while it is still this viewer's, and clears the active flag only when this viewer set it. This stops a cancelled or late-disposed viewer from resetting a newer viewer's arrow gate (I8).

The library's MutationObserver (`this.observer`) is created in the constructor, through `hack()` called from `init`. So `spreadsheet.observer?.disconnect()` right after `init` does reach it. That settles one of r1's open needs-human notes.

After the isolate commit and its revert, OfficePreview.tsx is identical to its r1 state. The product file list and the touch points are unchanged since r1: the FilePreview branch comes before the fallback, officeViewerFor shares OFFICE_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES, useFileNav does not import officeFiles and leaves PAGED_MIMES unchanged, and en.json and ja.json gain file.officeViewer.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Closing a DismissScrim menu by pressing on the Excel grid selects a cell (the library acts on mousedown) but does not activate the grid (the click is swallowed). The spec does not describe this case (R2).

The adapter now writes a private library field (`xs.sheet.focusing`) as well as reading it. If a library upgrade renamed it, both writes would silently do nothing, and the window paste, copy and key handlers would stay live after focus leaves the grid or after unmount.
regression_risks: None of the r1 fixes is covered by a test (R1). A later edit can remove the `focusing` release or the ownership check with CI still green.

After dispose, the old Sheet's window click handler still sets `focusing = detachedOverlayer.contains(target)`, which is always false. I9 therefore depends on the release in dispose and on the detached overlayer, and neither is tested.
test_coverage: The fix commits since r1 (e0a561429, caf19847a, beae9a97a) change no test file.

The arrow-key tests reach `onFocusIn` only through a focusable outside button. The probe path (a click outside on a non-focusable element) and the `focusing` release cannot be observed with the current mocks, which have no `xs`.
Since r1, coverage of I1–I8, I11 and I14 is unchanged. I read FilePreview.test.tsx and officeMimes.test.ts only at their changed hunks.

trajectory: Round 1 (e0a561429) replaced the synthetic body click with a direct write to the library's private `focusing` flag. That removed a mechanism, the page-wide event. The same round added a new ownership-aware release (`releaseOfficeGrid`, with conditions on probe identity and wasActive), which is one new piece of state logic. Round 2 (caf19847a) added a prediction, `isolate`, on the theory that stacking order caused a menu-dismiss click to select a cell. Round 3 (beae9a97a) removed that prediction because the theory was wrong (the scrim has pointer-events: none and selection starts on mousedown). No round adds a branch or state that the round before it also added. The net change since r1 is one mechanism removed (the synthetic click) and one ownership guard added. The menu-dismiss defect that round 2 targeted is still open (R2). The flip-flop in rounds 2 and 3 shows patching by guesswork on that one issue, not a design that keeps being patched.
